subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply-button/select clicks become synthetic inbound reply turns, or should heartbeat remain the delivery owner for Slack interaction events?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes ownership across Slack interaction ingestion, heartbeat prompt consumption, reply delivery, and in-flight session conflict handling; the issue is already marked as needing maintainer/product decision.

options.title: Use Inbound Reply Turns
options.body: Route user-initiated Slack reply controls through the same inbound reply pipeline as normal Slack messages, with coalescing/retry behavior and live Slack proof.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat Owner
options.body: Keep the current heartbeat wake design but add explicit Slack interaction prompt rendering, reply-delivery guarantees, and conflict retry coverage so clicks are not silently lost.

options.title: Defer To Broader Channel Action Model
options.body: Pause this issue until a generic channel-action callback contract is designed, accepting that Slack reply controls remain fragile in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Use Inbound Reply Turns
recommendation.body: Route user-initiated Slack reply controls through the same inbound reply pipeline as normal Slack messages, with coalescing/retry behavior and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Slack interaction routing and the channel runtime boundary, and steipete has prior merged work in that exact area.
